assessment: Xing and colleagues used a combination of biochemical assays and cryo-EM to investigate the role of PME-1 in regulating PP2A, which plays an important role in tumorigenesis. Notably, they reveal here that PME-1 inserts an unstructured loop into the B-domain of the PPA2 holoenzyme and allosterically regulates the activity of the catalytic domain. This novel mechanism then plays a key role in controlling the cellular homeostasis of PP2A. Together, the work presented here provides new insights into mechanisms for an oncogenic function of PME-1 in regulating (inhibiting) p53 phosphorylation via PP2A-B56 holoenzymes under normal and DNA damage response conditions.
